page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server configured with an AMD EPYC 9575F processor featuring 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB per core. Graphics and parallel computing acceleration are delivered via two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, totaling 96 GB of VRAM. This instance operates on the KVM hypervisor and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, but does not feature any local storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across multiple compute and processing metrics. The server achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU evaluations. Cryptographic and vector operations are supported by AVX-512 and AES instruction sets. Memory performance is strong, with read-only large block bandwidth reaching 327.05 GB/sec, though Passmark memory scores place in the average tier. LLM inference benchmarks show top-tier execution for small 135M models and strong performance for medium 7B models, while large 70B models drop to average tier speeds.

From a resource density perspective, the server offers high compute and GPU capacity relative to its hardware class, though the CPU allocation is shared. The absence of local storage represents a key architectural tradeoff, requiring external network storage solutions for persistent data. This configuration is highly suited for GPU-accelerated workloads such as machine learning training, medium-scale LLM inference, data science pipelines, and high-throughput database operations.
description: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-2xL40S is a high-capacity GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 32 physical cores, 384.0 GB of system memory, and two NVIDIA L40S GPUs providing 96 GB of total VRAM. The server delivers top-tier CPU performance, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng and Geekbench benchmarks, alongside strong memory bandwidth. LLM inference speeds are highly competitive for small and medium models, though performance scales down to average for large 70B models. A notable hardware tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage, requiring external storage attachments. This server is optimized for parallel computing tasks, machine learning inference, data science, and high-throughput database operations where massive GPU acceleration and substantial system memory are required.
